text.p: Continental Airlines chairman Gordon Bethune said on Wednesday that contract talks with pilots were going well and that a settlement was possible by October 1, a date favored by the union.
Bethune told Reuters in an interview that salary issues were the main sticking point, but he remained optimistic a quick agreement could be reached.

"I'm kind of happy with the way things are going. I always think things should be done faster, but the pilots themselves are saying October 1 now...if that's the date, let's get it on," he said after a ceremony in which eight Continental employees were presented with new Ford Explorers for perfect work attendance.
Contract negotiators are currently on break, but were set to resume talks on August 5 in Florida. They have been in discussions since April.
Bethune had hoped to have the contract by July 1, the date the current pact was supposed to expire, but no accord was reached.
Bethune said the two sides had resolved many issues apart from salary, but acknowledged that cash was the key point.
"You name me one time it wasn't the money...so it's a question of just doing the dance until the money gets resolved. It always gets resolved," he said.
Last week, Bethune told reporters the two sides were "probably about as far apart as Tokyo is to Paris" in their salary discussions.

The pilots say they earn 40 percent less than the industry average and want to be brought up to par now that once- troubled Continental is making money. The company earned $1.64 a share in the second quarter of 1997 on revenues of $1.79 billion.

The airline said the pilot demands would more than double their current pilot payroll of $400 million, but the pilots say Continental's offer of a 36 percent increase over several years is inadequate.
In a telephone message issued on Tuesday, the pilots warned that they were "dead serious about reaching an industry-standard contract...whatever it takes."
